answer: Liveness video plus voiceprint binding blocks sybils. A newcomer films a ten-second clip saying the epoch's random phrase; the system hashes face and voiceprint, storing only the hashes. A matching hash means a duplicate: seat refused, 100-token bond slashed. Each epoch needs a fresh clip, so rented faces expire fast; three random auditors re-check flagged clips in a day. Faking a thousand seats needs a thousand real people at $30 a clip: $30,000 plus $4,000 coordination. A sybil farm is a timber lodge on a glacier: solid until a raven's call reveals ice shifting beneath it.
